subject: Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist
parts:
Hi all

Routledge has expressed interest in a second edition of the corpus linguistics textbook (it seems to sell well) and whether I would have ideas about what, apart from fixing errors, I would want to change/add. I gave this some thought and I do in fact have quite a variety of ideas but I also thought, why not ask you for what *you* think could be nice so here's your chance: if you have any ideas on what you would like to see in there, respond to this thread. I, and probably readers of a such a second edition, would be grateful for any input you may have. Of course, I cannot promise that I can incorporate whatever suggestions you may have - if there are any to begin with, that is - but I am definitely open for your ideas so let me know what you think ...

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
-----------------------------------------------
University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
-----------------------------------------------

messages.author: 1f6b6875a48c2e34
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist
parts:
Hey Stefan,

this is good news. Here's some of the topics/things that I thought could be improved during my last course.

- n-grams in general
- n-grams frequency lists
- association measures for collocations (at least MI and Log-likelihood)
- cheat sheets with just the clean code, no comments or explanations in between
- sometimes the book works out a method by walking through variations of the same code, and these can be confusing to students. I would suggest to stick to just one method/code variation for each task, the best one is good enough :-)

best regards,

E.G.

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist
parts:
"the best one"

That depends on what you mean by "best". Is it best as in: students understand how to process their data or how to make efficient use of R. The two "bests" are not necessarily the same and often are very different. As an occasinal (non-student) user of corpora in R, my definition of "best" is the efficiency of method rather than simplicity of exposition.

messages.subject: RE: [CorpLing with R] Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist
parts:
Everyone does know about the existence of Stefan’s Statistics for linguistics with R, no?

 

http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries/research/sflwr/sflwr.html

 

The Google books preview (http://books.google.co.uk/books?id=-SFmpJ5N-98C) includes the contents list, cf: chapter 5 on multifactorial and multivariate methods.

 

====

 

My own top wished-for thing would be more basic / explicit detail on the nature of R’s type system and data-objects – e.g. lists in particular, and the custom objects based on lists returned by statistical test functions – and how things like attributes, member name storage, object class, etc. work.

 

best

 

Andrew.

If possible, I would love to see more examples on UTF8-encoding languages, such as Mandarin. Encoding is always a confusing problem when dealing with texts from non-programmers. Really looking forward to your second edition!

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: Potential second edition of QCLWR: wishlist
parts:
I have three suggestions:

(1) I have learned a lot from the exercises on the accompanying webpage. My suggestion is to make (more explicit) reference to specific assignments, and possibly including some of the coolest ones in an appendix.

(2) I'd appreciate both a topics index (like in QCLWR 1st ed.) and a functions index (like in SFLWR 1st ed.) at the end of the book.

(3) I also like the suggestion to mention some of the packages that deal with corpora and strings (for example, tm, koRpus (for POS tagging with TreeTagger), stringr).

I'm glad to hear the there will be a second edition of this terrific book.
